h: Karts in the Morning, Animals in the Afternoon
p: Dunstable's big neighbour in the days-out stakes is ZSL Whipsnade Zoo, sitting up on the Chiltern escarpment just outside town. It's huge, with animals in big open paddocks, and it pairs nicely with a session if you've got a family of mixed ages. The speed freaks get their race, the animal lovers get their elephants, and everyone's happy.
If you're doing both, get the karting done early. The zoo needs a good chunk of the day to do it justice, so a morning race followed by an afternoon there makes sense.

For groups without kids, Dunstable Downs is ideal for a walk after the race. On a clear day you can see for miles, and there's usually something going on in the sky, from kites to gliders from the London Gliding Club below.
Whatever you choose, a race and a big walk on the Downs is a hard combination to beat for a Bedfordshire day out.

As with all karting, book ahead at weekends and in the school holidays. Bring water, wear flat shoes and give yourself enough time to check in without a rush. Luton is just next door, so it's easy to reach by road or via Luton's railway connections.
